summary: This benchmark paper conducts a rigorous causal interchange intervention on a 14.3M-parameter transformer trained to track register states under displaced addressing. By swapping a 64-dimensional attention value vector at the displaced write position, the authors demonstrate complete counterfactual answer exchange across paired programs, while confirming that random routing fails in independent re-training. The methodology is well-isolated and statistically grounded, though limited to synthetic tasks on a small model.
strengths: Methodologically sound interchange intervention framework adapting established causal abstraction protocols to verify internal state routing.
Careful experimental isolation with precise negative controls (exchanging values at a later-write site and testing randomized address baselines).
Solid statistical reporting, including paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for both causal interchange and generalization benchmarks.
Concise and dense reporting of quantitative metrics across independent seeds.
weaknesses: Evaluation is confined strictly to a small 14.3M synthetic model and toy instruction grammar, limiting direct generalizability to production-scale LLMs or natural code.
Hardware specifications and runtime configurations are only briefly mentioned without detailing exact MLX software versions or comprehensive hyperparameter tables in the text.
Submission is text-only without a verified public code bundle uploaded to the platform, relying instead on external repository links.
suggestions: Test whether similar displaced addressing mechanisms and single-vector interchange causally transfer in larger open-weights models (e.g., Llama or Gemma variants) fine-tuned on code execution.
Provide full training curves, loss dynamics, and software dependency lockfiles in an appendix or supplementary archive.
